title: Nested Loops and Patterns
description: A loop inside a loop: grids, tables, triangles and charts.

content.value: A loop body can hold anything, even another loop. Then the inner loop runs **all the way through** on every single turn of the outer one.

content.real: A clock: the minute hand goes all the way round for each step of the hour hand
content.text: The outer counter changes slowly, the inner one changes fast.

steps.note: `col` becomes 4. `4 <= 3` is false: the inner loop is finished.
Outer loop, turn 2. The inner `col` is gone; a fresh one starts next.
`row` becomes 3. `3 <= 2` is false: everything is done.

content.title: Watch a 2 x 3 nested loop
content.outro: 2 outer turns x 3 inner turns = 6 lines.

content.question: How many times does this print Hi?
content.explain: Nesting multiplies: 3 outer turns, each running 4 inner turns. 3 x 4 = 12.

content.value: Nesting multiplies the work. Two loops to 1000 is a million turns. Three is a billion, which keeps a computer busy for a while.
content.title: Not free

content.value: Anything laid out in rows and columns needs two loops: grids, tables, seating plans, calendars. The trick is where you end each line.

items.title: After the inner loop
Inside the inner loop

content.title: Where does println go?
content.caption: Inside the outer loop but outside the inner one, `println()` ends the line once per row.
`row` changes slowly, `col` changes fast. For neat columns, print a tab `"\t"` instead of a space.

content.question: What is the second line of output?
content.explain: On the second outer turn `a` is 2, and the inner loop prints 2 x 1, 2 x 2 and 2 x 3.

content.value: The inner loop does not have to count to the same number every time. Use the outer counter as the inner limit, and the rows change length.

content.title: The triangle trick
content.caption: On row 1 the inner loop runs once. On row 5 it runs five times.
Turn the outer loop around (`row = rows; row >= 1; row--`) and the triangle stands on its head. Print `star + " "` instead and you get a number triangle.

content.value: A centred pyramid needs **two** inner loops per row. On row `r` of `n`, print `n - r` spaces, then `2 * r - 1` stars: 1, 3, 5, 7.

content.caption: The two inner loops run one after the other. Each finishes before the next starts, and only the `println` at the end closes the line.

content.value: The same shape does real work. Here the outer loop reads one score per turn, and the inner loop draws it as a bar: a chart.

content.title: One turn of the chart loop

content.caption: Sample run: 2 scores, 73 and 40, draw `73 | *******` and `40 | ****`. Whole-number division `score / 10` rounds each bar down to a sensible length.

items.sub: Inside the inner loop, every item gets its own line.
Two nested loops both using `i` will not compile.

items.sub: That is the difference between a rectangle and a triangle.

quiz.question: In a nested loop, how often does the inner loop run all the way through?
options: Once for every turn of the outer loop
Once for every turn of the inner loop
quiz.explain: The inner loop is an instruction in the outer block, so it starts again from its own first value on every outer turn.

quiz.question: Where must `System.out.println()` go to end each row of a grid?
options: Inside the outer loop but after the inner loop
quiz.explain: Once per outer turn is once per row. Inside the inner loop it would end the line after every single item.

quiz.question: What does `for (int star = 1; star <= row; star++)` give you?
options: A row whose length grows with the outer counter, making a triangle
A square, because every row is the same length
quiz.explain: The inner limit is the outer counter, so row 1 gets one star and row 5 gets five.

quiz.question: How many times does the innermost block run for two loops of 1 to 100 each?
quiz.explain: Nesting multiplies the counts: 100 times 100. It is why nested loops over big ranges get slow quickly.

quiz.question: Why do a pyramid's rows need two inner loops?
options: One prints the leading spaces and the other prints the stars
Because a pyramid has two halves
Because one loop cannot print spaces
quiz.explain: They run one after the other on each row: `rows - row` spaces to push it inwards, then `2 * row - 1` stars.
